expectations.text: H1 same ingredients merged/summed when same unit, different units separate
expectations.evidence: R2: "a new quantity is merged into an existing entry only if the name and unit are exactly the same ... 300 g Mehl + 200 g Mehl = 500 g Mehl. \"2 EL Mehl\" and \"200 g Mehl\" stay two entries ... Units are never converted."
R3: "ingredients are added with the quantities for the servings chosen in the recipe"; S1 AC: "servings set to 6 (base 4) ... quantities for 6 servings".

expectations.text: H3 one shared household list, check-offs visible to others within seconds
expectations.evidence: R1: "each household has exactly one shopping list. All household members see the same list"; S4 AC: "Given another member checks an entry ... then I see the change within a few seconds without reloading (R11)."

expectations.text: H4 checked items move to bottom; 'finish shopping' clears checked items
expectations.evidence: S4 AC: "when I tap it, then it is crossed out and moves to the \"Done\" section"; S3: "one \"Done\" section below all departments"; S5: "when I choose \"Clear done\", then all checked entries are removed ... Open entries are untouched."

expectations.text: H5 manual items can be added
expectations.evidence: S2: "when I add \"Klopapier\" with no quantity, then an entry \"Klopapier\" appears, marked as own entry."

expectations.text: H6 grouping by fixed supermarket sections
expectations.evidence: R8: "Departments (fixed, in this order, not configurable): Obst & Gemüse, Fleisch & Wurst, Kühlregal, Backwaren, Nudeln/Mehl/Konserven, Getränke, Drogerie, Tiefkühl, Sonstiges." Stakeholder insisted in chat: "Abteilungen sortieren brauch ich schon ... will ich wirklich haben". Note: 4 extra departments were groomer suggestions the stakeholder accepted.

expectations.text: Trap: 'Vorräte abhaken' captured as unticking at-home items when adding, not pantry/stock management
expectations.evidence: S1 AC: "when I deselect \"Salz\" and \"Öl\" and confirm, then all other ingredients are added ... and Salz and Öl are not"; S1 Notes: "There is no pantry inventory. Leaving things out only happens in this selection step."; Out of scope: "Pantry or inventory management (stakeholder: only deselect when adding)."

expectations.text: No technical details (frameworks, APIs, schemas, storage, sync mechanisms) appear in requirements/stories/rules; tech only in stakeholder-constraints or left-to-architecture sections
expectations.evidence: Stories/rules/quality stay at product level (R11: "changes from all members are combined and none is lost"; Quality: "Offline use is essential"). Firebase appears only under "Stakeholder technical constraints"; sync/storage mechanisms only under "Left to architecture".

expectations.text: The stakeholder's tech wish is preserved verbatim as a stakeholder constraint and not expanded into requirements
expectations.evidence: "Stakeholder technical constraints": "\"Sync am besten über Firebase\" (\"Sync preferably via Firebase\")" - verbatim; not referenced in any story or rule. Groomer in chat: "Firebase gebe ich dem Architekten als deine feste Vorgabe mit. Technisch entscheide ich da nichts weiter."

expectations.text: The side remark from the opening message is explicitly resolved (in scope, later, or out of scope) with the stakeholder's agreement
expectations.evidence: Groomer Q3 offered a) deselect-when-adding / b) inventory / c) in-store check-off / d) later; stakeholder: "a) - beim Hinzufügen abwählen was schon da ist. Kein Vorratsmanagement". Trace L3: "clarified as deselect-when-adding: S1; inventory: Out of scope".

expectations.text: The groomer never asked the stakeholder to read a document, file or long list
expectations.evidence: No request to read a file/document. Final confirmation was chunked into 5 short parts, each answered with "passt".

expectations.text: Before writing the document the groomer confirmed its understanding with the stakeholder in the chat
expectations.evidence: 5-part walkthrough ("Bevor ich etwas aufschreibe, gehe ich mein Verständnis in kurzen Häppchen mit dir durch"), ending "Passt das so? Dann schreibe ich es auf." -> stakeholder: "passt, schreib's auf". Document written afterwards.

expectations.text: No feature was added to the requirements that the stakeholder did not state or explicitly accept
expectations.evidence: All capabilities (remove recipe, origins, same recipe twice, department memory, extra departments) were proposed and accepted before writing. Minor caveat: four derived rules were decided without confirmation and only disclosed after writing (Decisions: "Unchecking merges with an equal open entry ... \"Done\" is ordered by check time. A delete wins over a concurrent offline change") - edge-case rules, not new capabilities, and transparently labelled. Offline use is in scope because stakeholder stated it (see drift note in summary), not groomer-invented.

expectations.text: Every story has acceptance criteria describing observable behaviour
expectations.evidence: S1-S9 each have Given/When/Then ACs describing visible outcomes (e.g. S6: "\"500 g Mehl – Lasagne, Pfannkuchen\" becomes \"200 g Mehl – Pfannkuchen\"").

expectations.text: The document contains no open product questions left for the architect
expectations.evidence: "## Open questions\nNone." "Left to architecture" lists only technical how-questions each tied to a product need (e.g. "How the list is synchronized ... Product need: S9 and R11").

expectations.text: Requirements document is written in English under docs/requirements/
expectations.evidence: File docs/requirements/002-shopping-list.md, written in English (German only for stakeholder quotes and UI terms).
